$comment: What the Librarian reads from a model's reply, as every implementation of the Librarian must read it. Semiont's Librarian (apps/librarian: replies.py) runs every case, in apps/librarian/tests/test_reply_cases.py, and fails on a difference; a Librarian in another language runs the same file. Two prompts are asked for elements: the reply to each is an array, and a provider holds every element of it to a JSON Schema, which specs/src/librarian/prompt-cases.json states. A schema of that kind says an element's shape and no more: not that a number is whole, or from 0 to 1, or the number of a candidate that was shown. So there are two readers, and a case's `reader` says which it is of. `elements` is the array a model answered. An element that is not what was asked for gives nothing, and is no error. THE READER OF `scores` reads the reply to a score prompt, which listed `candidates` candidates, numbered from 1. `scores` is what is read: each item is the number of a `candidate` and the `score` read for it. A candidate that is not in `scores` has no score read. The rule: an element gives a score when it is an object whose `candidate` is a whole number from 1 to `candidates`, written with a fraction of nothing or with none, and whose `score` is a number from 0 to 1, both ends included. Where two elements give a score for one candidate, the later is the one read. THE READER OF `suggestions` reads the reply to a reference-suggestions prompt. `suggestions` is the list read, or null where nothing is read. The rule: an element gives a suggestion when it is an object whose `suggestion` is a text with something in it other than white space, which is what Unicode gives the White_Space property; the suggestion is that text without the white space at its two ends. The first three are read, in the reply's order. A reply that gives none answers null, and the gathered context then states no suggestions: an empty list is never answered. A REPLY THAT IS NO ARRAY, and one cut off at the token limit, are not read at all: each is a failure of the request of the model, and is no case here. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: each element that gives a candidate's number and a score is read
a reply with no element gives no score
a candidate the reply leaves out has no score, and the others have theirs
the scores 0 and 1 are read: both ends are included
a score above 1 and one below 0 give nothing
a number that is none of the candidates' gives nothing: 0, and one more than were listed
a candidate's number that is not whole names no candidate
a whole number written with a fraction of nothing is the candidate's number
where two elements score one candidate, the later is read
a score written as text is no number, and gives nothing
a candidate's number written as text names no candidate
true and false are no numbers: neither is a candidate's number or a score
an element that lacks its candidate or its score gives nothing
an element that is no object gives nothing, and the elements beside it are read
what an element states beside its candidate and its score is not read
each element's suggestion is read, in the reply's order

elements.suggestion: Map the crossing at Yellow Banks

suggestions: Map the crossing at Yellow Banks

cases.why: the first three suggestions are read, and no more
a reply with no element gives no suggestions at all
the white space at the two ends of a suggestion is dropped, and what is inside it is kept
a suggestion of white space alone, and an empty one, are dropped, and do not count toward the three
a reply whose every suggestion is empty gives none at all, and not an empty list
a suggestion is its text as written: a bullet or a number a model wrote before it is kept
a suggestion that is no text gives nothing
an element that is no object, and one with no suggestion, give nothing, and the elements beside them are read
what an element states beside its suggestion is not read
